title_en: QUAKE — INSIGHT & THE INSIDE OF MARS
description: An interactive field guide to NASA's InSight lander (2018–2022): the SEIS seismometer under its wind and thermal shield, 1,319 marsquakes and the magnitude 4.7 S1222a, meteoroid impacts heard by SEIS and found by MRO, the crust, mantle and a liquid core revised from 1,830 km to about 1,650–1,675 km, the HP³ mole that could not dig, and the dust that ended the mission.
og: Weigh a marsquake, send rays through a layered Mars to find the core's shadow, see why InSight's mole had no grip, and watch dust drain the solar panels: InSight's four years on Mars, interactive and checked against the mission's published results.
brand: QUAKE — TECHNICAL FIELD GUIDE / ТЕХНИЧЕСКИЙ СПРАВОЧНИК
llms: NASA's InSight lander (2018–2022): the SEIS seismometer and its wind shield, 1,319 marsquakes and the M4.7 S1222a, meteoroid impacts heard seismically and confirmed by MRO, crust, mantle and a liquid core revised from 1,830 km to ~1,650–1,675 km (molten silicate layer; 2025 inner-core claim), the HP³ mole's friction failure and the dust that ended the mission — with a moment calculator, a toy ray tracer fitted to S1000a, a mole-friction model and a solar-power model.

freshness.claim: Core radius "as of November 2026": liquid core ~1,650–1,675 km under a molten silicate layer
Solid inner core (613 ± 67 km, 2025) still debated, not independently confirmed
NSSDC Mars fact sheet still lists 1,830 km with a 1,650–1,675 km footnote (retrieved 2026-11-12)
1,319 marsquakes = NASA's end-of-mission count; the Marsquake Service reference catalogue (being finalised in 2025) lists over 1,900 events — update when the catalogue paper appears
